item.title: Banks Offload Risk from Leveraged ETFs With Exotic ‘Crash Puts’
item.description: Leveraged ETFs that offer the tantalizing prospect of doubling or tripling the daily returns of an individual stock are famously risky for investors who buy them.

item.title: ANZ, NAB Among Banks Funding Blackstone HSBC Book Buy, AFR Says
item.description: ANZ Group Holdings Ltd. and National Australia Bank Ltd. are among lenders bankrolling Blackstone Inc.’s A$36 billion ($25.3 billion) purchase of HSBC Holdings Plc’s Australian retail loan portfolio, the Australian Financial Review reported Sunday, citing unnamed sources.

item.title: Bomb Kills Three, Injures 21 at Restaurant on Moscow’s Kudrinskaya Square
item.description: Three people were killed and 21 injured after a bomb was detonated in an upscale restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday night, according to Russia’s National Anti-Terrorism Committee.

item.title: South Korea Issues Heat Wave Alert as Temperature Hits Record
item.description: South Korea issued emergency heat wave instructions as the country sweltered, with its highest temperature on record reported in the southeastern city of Yangsan.

item.title: AI Is Creating a Two-Speed Jobs Market in the UK, Indeed Says
item.description: UK employers are creating jobs for experienced staff with artificial intelligence skills and cutting back elsewhere, according to new figures that show how the technology is starting to create a two-track labor market.

item.title: Katayama to Say Japan, US Are Coordinating to Curb Yen Weakness
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama is set to announce as early as Monday that Tokyo and Washington are coordinating on steps in the foreign exchange market to curb the yen’s weakness, a person familiar with the situation said.

item.title: Trump Says US to Cancel Iran Attack Subject to a Rapid Deal
item.description: President Donald Trump said the US will hold off new strikes against Iran after the Islamic Republic and other Middle Eastern nations told him they are working toward a deal.

item.title: Malaysia Minister Sees Stable Second-Half Growth, Bernama Says
item.description: Malaysia’s Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the country’s economy is expected to remain strong in the second half of the year as the government maintains stable supplies of oil, Bernama reported.

item.title: Saudi Prince Concerned Over Trump’s Iran Strike Plan: Axios
item.description: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman told President Donald Trump in a call that he was concerned over the US’s plans for new strikes against Iran, Axios reported, citing people familiar with the conversation.

item.title: Crushed by Kospi Rout, Angry Koreans Rip Lee and Vow Not to Buy
item.description: South Korea’s retail traders have long built a reputation for embracing risk. Yet July’s punishing reversal in the Kospi has rattled even this battle-hardened cohort, exposing the limits of their tolerance for volatility.

item.title: US Job Growth to Pick Up After Disappointing June
item.description: Employers in the US likely stepped up their pace of hiring in July, showing a steady appetite for workers despite the overhang of geopolitical concerns and elevated inflation.

item.title: AI Loan Market Sees Investor Demands Rise, Borrowers Offer Better Terms
item.description: Loan investors are pushing back for the first time in years, in a shift that will probably translate to higher borrowing costs for everyone from private equity firms to deeply indebted AI companies.

item.title: Zepto Turns to Private Funding With IPO Plans on Hold for Now
item.description: Zepto Ltd said it agreed on a private share sale to major investors as the Indian quick-commerce firm pushed back plans for an initial public offering after failing to secure its anticipated valuation.

item.title: Peru’s Inflation Tops Forecasts as Food, Transport Prices Climb
item.description: Inflation in Peru’s capital accelerated faster than expected in July as food and transport prices climbed, staying above the target range for a fifth straight month.

item.title: Romania Narrowly Averts Junk Rating on Debt Amid Budget Scrutiny
item.description: Romania narrowly avoided having its debt downgraded to junk status, which the country’s acting finance chief called a warning to overcome the current political deadlock and continue with budget reforms.

item.title: Exxon, Chevron Warn Fuel Prices to Endure as War Knocks Refining
item.description: High fuel prices are likely to stick around even if oil prices drop in the coming months as the wars in Russia and Middle East leave global refining capacity critically short, ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. and Chevron Corp. warned.

item.title: Warsh’s Silent Treatment Has S&P Traders Bracing for Wild Swings
item.description: A relentless run of uncertainty, from war to tariff fights to inflation that refuses to die, has challenged investors this year. Now they have to balance another risk: A Federal Reserve that won’t tell them what it’s thinking.

item.title: Phoenix Extends Record-Breaking Heat as West Faces Fire Threat
item.description: Phoenix has had a record-breaking run of high temperatures and that streak will continue through the coming week, as heat and fire risks spread across the wider US West.

item.title: Fed’s Credibility Test and J&J’s New Bet
item.description: The Fed’s decision on rates could have been a non-event

item.title: AI Isn’t a Catch-All Trade for Stocks in This Earnings Season
item.description: Equity investors are learning a harsh lesson this corporate earnings season: Not all artificial intelligence trades are created equal.

item.title: Turkey Said to Extend Iraq Oil Pipeline Deal by One Year
item.description: Turkey reached an agreement with Iraq to extend an expired oil pipeline deal by one year and increase flows through it, ensuring supply through an exports route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Rising Fuel Prices Hit Americans Now Without Tax Refunds to Tap
item.description: When fuel costs jumped earlier in the Iran war, US consumers powered through it — with a hefty assist from federal tax refunds. Now they’re getting hit by another wave of higher gasoline prices, and the buffer is gone.

item.title: Bessent Misses Chance to Coordinate with a China-Wary Europe
item.description: There is an opportunity for a unified strategy with Europe. But the US is going it alone.

item.title: Tanker Carrying Qatari LNG Struck While Transiting Hormuz
item.description: A liquefied natural gas tanker carrying a shipment from Qatar was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to security intelligence firms and ship tracking data, threatening to further disrupt deliveries of the super-chilled fuel through the key waterway.

item.title: Indian Oil Buys Record Spot Market Crude on Mideast Supply Hit
item.description: Indian Oil Corp. bought a record share of its crude oil from the spot market in the April-June quarter after the US-Iran conflict upended supplies from the Middle East. The shift shows how geopolitical turmoil is forcing even the region’s biggest buyers to abandon long-established procurement strategies.

item.title: Europe’s Endless Heat Waves Imperil Once Reliable Power Sources
item.description: A series of blistering heat waves has weakened some of Europe’s most historically reliable sources of electricity, forcing the continent to lean more heavily on imported fossil fuels and variable renewable energy.

item.title: World Economy Latest: Central Banks Hold Rates Steady
item.description: Monetary policymakers from the US and the UK to Japan left interest rates unchanged this week as they assessed renewed inflation risks from higher energy costs and war in the Middle East.

item.title: How an Iron Ore Empire ‘Built on Trust’ Began to Sow Doubts
item.description: In a corporate presentation in December 2024, Radiant World boasted of its “diverse network” of suppliers and counterparties.

item.title: Germany’s Elusive Economic Revival Is Within Touching Distance
item.description: The long-awaited recovery of Europe’s largest economy is finally coming into view.

item.title: Bessent and the Fed Help Japan Reverse Months of Yen Losses
item.description: The US joined Japan in engineering one of the most notable rebounds in the yen since the currency began its years-long slide, a decline that’s stoked inflation in the Asian nation and rippled through global markets.
